pages.page_text:
Section/page heading: M.R.K.PANNEERSELVAM

FOREWORD

       With the noble aim of uplifting the livelihood of farmers who are
working tirelessly to eradicate hunger across the globe, as per the directive
of the Honorable  Chief  Minister, separate  agricultural budget  is being
presented in Tamil Nadu. The Department of Agriculture - Farmers Welfare
has presented five Agricultural budgets for the period from 2021-22 to
2025-26,  with numerous  welfare schemes which  are  being  effectively
implemented.

       The  Department  of  Agriculture  -  Farmers  Welfare  is  set  to
implement a wide range of impactful schemes in 2025-26, including the
Chief Minister’s Farmers Service Centres, Encouraging Summer Ploughing in
Rainfed Areas, Special Package scheme for Kuruvai Cultivation in Delta and
Non Delta districts, Tamil Nadu Millet Mission,  Hill Farmers Development
Scheme,  Village  Outreach  Campaign,  Maize  production  enhancement
Scheme,  Oilseeds  Mission,  Palmyrah  Development  Mission,  Nutrition
Farming  Mission,  Chief  Minister’s Mannuyir Kaathu Mannuyir Kaappom
Scheme, Integrated Coconut Development Scheme, Jackfruit Development
Mission,  Organic Farming  Clusters,  waiver  of  certification  charges  for
Organic Farming scheme to provide electric motor pumpsets at subsidy,
Agricultural Machinery Custom Hiring Centers, and the scheme to rejuvenate
open irrigation wells.

       The Citizen Charter, with details of the agricultural schemes to be
implemented  in 2025-26  through  the  Agriculture –  Farmers'  Welfare
Department, will be uploaded in the Government website, making it easily
accessible to the public.

          I am pleased that, the Citizen Charter for 2025-26 will prove to be a
valuable resource, offering significant benefits to everyone.



                          M.R.K.PANNEERSELVAM
                                 Minister for Agriculture – Farmers Welfare

6. TAMIL NADU AGRICULTURAL UNIVERSITY

     Tamil Nadu Agricultural University plays a vital role in enhancing the
farm income and productivity of crops through its multiple roles such as;
producing quality manpower for agricultural services by providing quality
education, addressing the field level problems through focused Agricultural
Research and transfer of promising technologies from lab to land besides,
supporting the Government on policy matters. The University also has Open
and  Distance  Learning and  Agri-business Development  Directorates  to
enhance the knowledge and alivelihood of farmers. TNAU also strives hard
to  promote  environmentally  sustainable  production  and  processing
technologies to compete  in the national and international markets. The
various services offered by TNAU to the farming community and the public
are given hereunder.


6. 1. Stake holders

   2.  Under-Graduate, Post-Graduate, Doctoral and Diploma students of
        agriculture and allied subjects

       University
   4.  Farm input producers and distributors
   5.  Agro-based entrepreneurs
   6.  Extension personnel of the development departments
   7.   Policy makers at State and National level
   8.  Collaborators from National and International organizations
   9.  General  public   in  need  of  capacity  building  in  agriculture,
        horticulture, food and nutrition.

6.6. Other Services to Farmers
      Quality seeds in agricultural and horticultural crops of TNAU varieties
were produced and distributed to the farmers. Trainings regarding seed
production aspects were also imparted to the farmers.

6.6.1. Production and supply of quality seeds and planting materials
     During 2024-25, a  total quantity  of 384.05 tonnes  of foundation
seeds, 53.28 tonnes  of  certified seeds and 563.43 tonnes  of  Truthful
Labelled Seeds (TFL) seeds in 175 varieties of principal crops were produced
and supplied  for the benefit of farmers. Apart from  this seedlings and
planting materials of various crops to the tune of 10.90 lakhs were produced
and distributed. During 2025-26,  it is targeted to produce approximately
897.2 tonnes of foundation seeds, 101.2 tonnes of certified seeds, 1195.1
tonnes of Truthful Labelled (TFL) Seeds and 26.8 lakhs seedlings and other
planting materials of various crops.

court cases of university. The Vigilance unit monitoring the code of conduct

Rules. The unit acts on the complaints received by probing and furnishing
the fats of the cases. The Law section under this unit deals with civil cases
